game: BUF@LV Week 6 2026 (kickoff time not in pack; LV +5, total 54, implied BUF 29.5 / LV 24.5; venue and weather not saved)

script.base: A 54 total with Buffalo favored by 5 is a competitive points game, not a slog and not a blowout: Buffalo leads by about a score late, James Cook keeps a lead-back carry share into a soft Raiders run front, and Las Vegas as the dog has to throw, with Brock Bowers (34 targets, 312 yards over weeks 3-5) as the first read. Pace stays up because both implied totals sit in the mid-20s.
script.flip1: Buffalo jumps up two scores early and runs clock. Cook's carries rise and Bills wideout yards stall (Shakir/Coleman/Moore), while Las Vegas abandons Ashton Jeanty (44 carries, 141 yards, 3.20 YPC in weeks 3-5) and throws more, which feeds Bowers until Buffalo sits starters.
script.flip2: Las Vegas leads or a Bills turnover forces a pass-heavy chase. Cook's rush line dies, Josh Allen throws more (he is already 22 carries / 148 rush yards in three games, so he can also steal explosive runs), and Jeanty's carries fall while his 17 targets can keep a rush-plus-rec line alive. A Raiders lead that turns into clock-killing runs is the version that unders Bowers.

injury_fallout: Source is the pre-game nflverse injury report only; inactives ~90 minutes before kick are not in the pack. LV DT Tonka Hemingway Out (concussion) is the run-game fallout: the interior defender in front of Cook is gone and no backup DT is named, so Buffalo's rush efficiency is the side that gains. LV WR Dont'e Thornton Jr. Out (hamstring) and TE Carter Runyon Out (foot) do not show up in the weeks 3-5 target tree (Bowers 34, Jeanty 17, Tre Tucker 17, Michael Mayer 14, Cody White 11), so those absences look already priced into Tucker/White/Mayer/Bowers rather than a fresh sleeper bump. LV C Trey Zuhn III Questionable (knee): if he sits, Jeanty efficiency falls and Kirk Cousins faces more pressure (quick throws up, deep yards down); not banked. BUF WR DJ Moore Questionable (shoulder; 12 targets / 78 yards / 145 air in three games) and WR Josh Palmer Questionable (shoulder; 4 targets / 3 yards): if either is inactive, Khalil Shakir (14 targets) and Keon Coleman (11) gain looks, but both are still questionable so that bump is not used. BUF DE Ed Oliver and DE T.J. Sanders Questionable, and CB Dee Alford Questionable (ankle): if the ends sit, Las Vegas protection improves; Alford is not confirmed as anyone's primary defender. No Bills offensive lineman is listed out.

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack (no coverage charting). Location splits only: Las Vegas middle 9.11 YPA on 27 attempts is the soft zone, with left 7.69 (70) and right 7.65 (63). Buffalo is even: left 7.12 (74), middle 7.63 (43), right 7.43 (84).
matchup.pressure: Las Vegas blitzes 25%; Buffalo EPA/db is 0.39 vs blitz and 0.33 vs no blitz, so Allen is fine either way and slightly better when blitzed. Buffalo blitzes 34%; Las Vegas EPA/db is 0.13 vs blitz and 0.15 vs none, a small Cousins dip, not a collapse. Pressure that gets home would cut deep yards (Coleman 203 air yards on 11 targets; Tucker 219 air on 17) and lift RB/TE checkdowns (Ty Johnson 10 targets, -9 air; Jeanty 17 targets, 31 air).
matchup.bleeds: Las Vegas run defense allows 5.40 YPC and 20 runs of 10+ over 5 games, plus 15 passes of 20+ for 173 yards. Buffalo run defense allows 3.99 YPC and 16 runs of 10+, and has given up more explosives (22 passes of 20+ for 212). Buffalo does not show a location bleed.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Cook's carry monopoly (61 of the Bills' RB carries in three games, ahead of Ray Davis 3/5) into Las Vegas's 5.40 YPC front with Hemingway out. Bowers is the target king but Buffalo's YPA splits do not give him a matching hole. Shakir's short game (57 air yards on 14 targets) would fit the Raiders' middle 9.11, but a 6-yard game sits inside his three-game 168 yards and a Buffalo lead stalls WR yards, so he is not carded.

form: Avoiding season averages. Cook last4 rush yards 135, 154, 75, 111; 154+75+111=340 matches his weeks 3-5 total, so the 75-yard miss is inside the recent window, not an old outlier, while the role is still 20.3 carries a game at 5.57 YPC. Allen's three-game rush split is 23, 4 and 121 (the 72 is the extra game), a spike not a trend. Davis last4 rush 3, 3, 2. Shakir's three-game yards include a 6 (with 82 and 80); Coleman’s include 7 and 37 under a 39.5 line plus a 116. Kincaid’s recent window is 38, 7, 7 against a 54 line. Bowers is 116, 86, 110, all over 80.5, on 34 targets. Jeanty’s three-game rushes are 56, 58 and 27 (3.20 YPC) with receiving 15/37/68/50 mixed in. Tucker’s three-game receiving is 43, 44, 41, barely over 39.5. No new OC, QB change, or prior-season fallback is indicated; Cousins is the Las Vegas QB on the saved rush prop.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Cook over 93.5 lost. Buffalo trailed or played pass-first, Cook landed nearer the 75 already inside his 154/75/111 three-game split than the 135 or 154, and Las Vegas loaded the box even with Hemingway out so efficiency fell under 4.5 on something like 18 carries. Allen took the explosive runs the way his 121-yard game shows he can. A late Cook scratch or snap limit would do it too, and that inactive list is not in the pack. That counter is real, which is why this is flagged for a human and not auto-sized, but it is not stronger than 20 carries into a 5.40 YPC defense in a Buffalo -5 script, so the leg is not cut. Bowers was left off because a lean that the pass defense does not actually bleed, with only a 5.5-yard cushion under his worst recent game, loses the red-team check.
slip_story: One-story slip only: Buffalo leads and runs, soft Raiders front. Single leg, James Cook rush yards over 93.5. Do not add Bills WR overs (Shakir, Coleman, Moore, Palmer), which need the pass-heavy flip, and do not add a game under against a 54 total. The correlated dog-pass piece would have been Bowers receiving over, and it was dropped. No TD legs, no second market on Cook.
